newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech premier plays down chance of early elections.
newsitem.headline: Czech premier plays down chance of early elections.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus played down on Tuesday the possibility of early lower house elections if his Civic Democratic Party (ODS) performs strongly in Senate polls starting this weekend.

Klaus noted that ODS vice-chairman Ivan Pilip had poured cold water last week on speculation that the three-party coalition might be tempted to try to regain the majority it lost in lower house elections in June.
The minority government still had to push through a wide range of reforms, he told a news conference.
"I cannot imagine the possibility of solving the healthcare (crisis), the higher education law or the question of the banking system and its privatisation while there are more elections," he said.
Klaus indicated that the government did not want to duck its responsibilities.

The Senate elections, the first round of which will be held on Friday and Saturday, are the first electoral test of Czech public opinion since the inconclusive June polls when the centre-right coalition fell two seats short of a majority.

The Senate has few powers but analysts say that if ODS does well, Klaus might provoke a confrontation with the opposition Social Democrats to bring forward elections, which are not due until the year 2000.

Conversely, Klaus might be forced to resign if he loses the race for the newly-created Senate, meaning he is outvoted in both chambers of parliament, they say. -- Jan Lopatka, Prgaue newsroom, (42 2) 24 23 0003
